headword: {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}

definitions.explanation: A company whose ownership and/or management is concentrated in the hands of a single family or a small number of related families. The term covers everything from small neighborhood shops to large publicly listed corporations in which the founding family retains a controlling stake or holds key executive posts.

examples.japanese: うちは{同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}だ。
{日本|にほん}には{老舗|しにせ}の{同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Japan has many long-established family-owned companies.

examples.japanese: {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}には、{意思|いし}{決定|けってい}が{速|はや}いという{利点|りてん}がある。
examples.english: Family-owned companies have the advantage of being able to make decisions quickly.

examples.japanese: {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}では、{後継者|こうけいしゃ}{問題|もんだい}や{親族|しんぞく}{間|かん}の{対立|たいりつ}が{経営|けいえい}{上|じょう}の{大|おお}きな{課題|かだい}となりやすい。
examples.english: In family-owned companies, succession problems and conflicts among relatives easily become major management challenges.

notes:
Composed of {同族|どうぞく} (same family; same clan) and {企業|きぎょう} (enterprise; company). The {族|ぞく} here refers to the family lineage rather than ethnicity.

USAGE:
A neutral, descriptive term used in business news, accounting and tax contexts, and corporate governance discussions. Note the specialized tax-law sense: under Japan's Corporation Tax Act, a {同族会社|どうぞくがいしゃ} is a company in which three or fewer shareholders together own more than 50% of the shares — a status that triggers special anti-tax-avoidance rules. Outside of tax law, the everyday meaning is broader and synonymous with 'family business.' The reading {どうぞく} is fixed; do not confuse with {同属|どうぞく} 'of the same genus.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}を{経営|けいえい}する: to run a family business
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}を{継|つ}ぐ: to inherit/take over a family business
- {大手|おおて}{同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}: a major family-owned company
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}の{後継者|こうけいしゃ}: successor in a family business

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {同族会社|どうぞくがいしゃ}: family company — narrower technical term used in tax law
- {家族経営|かぞくけいえい}: family management — emphasizes management by family members; often a smaller scale
- {老舗|しにせ}: long-established business — emphasizes age and tradition; many {老舗|しにせ} are also {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}
- ファミリービジネス: family business — katakana loanword, common in MBA-style writing
